paras: The lynching of John Kirkland was the killing of a prisoner by masked men near the jail at Nashville, Arkansas, on the night of October 8, 1888. Kirkland, accused of firing on a local physician, was taken from a constable and shot to death. Brief wire dispatches carried the story to papers in Dakota Territory and Kansas.

According to a Nashville dispatch, Kirkland and Dr. Chisolm had a dispute on Saturday over some work Kirkland had done for the doctor. A Kansas City version spelled the name Chisholm and described him as "a prominent physician of the town." Both accounts said Kirkland then fired on the doctor, the Nashville report stating that he waylaid him that night and missed.

The Nashville dispatch said a posse tried to arrest Kirkland, but he defended himself and escaped, and he was not captured until the night of October 8. He was turned over to a constable, who set out with him for the jail a few hundred yards away. On the way the constable was met by several masked men armed with Winchester rifles, who took charge of the prisoner and told the constable to ride on. They then "riddled Kirkland with bullets, killing him instantly."
The Kansas City wire said the masked men took him into the woods before shooting him.
No report of an inquest, arrests or a grand jury inquiry appears in the coverage.

The Press and Daily Dakotaian of Yankton printed the Kansas City wire on October 11 under the headline "Killed by a Mob," describing the killers as "a mob of citizens." A week later the Barton County Democrat of Great Bend, Kansas, ran the fuller Nashville dispatch as "A Desperate Character Killed." That version closed with the remark that "Kirkland was known as a desperate character," a line that framed the victim rather than the masked men. Neither paper named the race of Kirkland or his killers, and neither commented on the killing.

The two dispatches differ on the arrest: the Kansas City wire said Kirkland was arrested right after the failed attempt, while the Nashville report, written closer to the scene, said he first escaped a posse.

reader.title: Lynching of John Kirkland
bases: Masked men took Kirkland from a constable on the way to jail and shot him to death (A1, A2).

Kirkland, arrested for allegedly firing on a physician, was taken from a constable by a 'mob of masked men' (A1), 'several masked men with Winchester' (A2), and riddled with bullets; the killing punished an alleged crime without any legal process.
Two separately worded dispatches, from Kansas City (A1) and Nashville (A2), agree on the core event, though both may derive from the same original Arkansas report.

accounts.label: Nashville, Ark. dispatch (Oct. 9)
accounts.gist: After a Saturday quarrel over work, Kirkland waylaid Dr. Chisolm and missed, escaped a posse, was captured on the night of Oct. 8, and was taken from the constable near the jail by several masked men with Winchesters, who shot him dead.

accounts.label: Kansas City wire (Oct. 10)
accounts.gist: A few hours after a quarrel, Kirkland tried to assassinate Dr. Chisholm, failed and was arrested; on the way to jail a mob of masked men seized him, took him into the woods and riddled him with bullets.

framing.detail: A Dakota daily ran the Kansas City wire brief under 'Killed by a Mob', calling the killers 'a mob of citizens' without comment.

A Kansas weekly ran the Nashville dispatch under 'A Desperate Character Killed', closing with the line that Kirkland 'was known as a desperate character', which leaned toward the mob's side without endorsing the killing.
